rationale: Direct match for the fuzzy-matching pipeline concern. RapidFuzz is a mature, MIT-licensed Python/C++ fuzzy string matching library (v3.14.5) that provides the full FuzzyWuzzy-compatible API surface (ratio, partial_ratio, token_sort_ratio, token_set_ratio, WRatio, QRatio) plus extensive edit-distance metrics (Levenshtein, Damerau-Levenshtein, Hamming, Jaro, Jaro-Winkler, Indel, LCSseq, OSA, Prefix, Postfix). The library is written primarily in C++ with Cython bindings and provides SIMD-accelerated paths (AVX2, SSE2) with pure-Python fallback. It includes batch matching via cdist/cpdist, extract/extractOne/extract_iter, and supports multiprocessing (workers parameter). The test suite has 23 test files including property-based hypothesis tests. 221 source files and 40 directories reflect deep architecture (C++ algorithms in metrics.hpp, Cython wrapper layers, CPU feature detection, build system with scikit-build-core and optional Taskflow parallelism). Heritage is declared_prior as the task states this is a direct pipeline candidate per prior assignment. Tier S because the library is the premier fuzzy matching dependency for a scraping pipeline extracting structured product specs -- its core function (string similarity on product names, descriptions, specs) is a foundational requirement, the architectural depth (C++ with SIMD tiers, multi-algorithm support, process module for bulk matching) is maximal among fuzzy matching libraries, and it has no directly comparable alternative in terms of performance and API completeness.
limitations: No formal architecture/design documents in-repo; architecture is inferred from build system and C++ headers only
Has no built-in scraping-specific heuristics (e.g. product attribute extraction, price parsing)
DamerauLevenshtein metrics are marked experimental in the C++ header (rf::experimental:: namespace)
cdist parallel workers (multiprocessing) only available via C-API, not pure Python fallback
Optional numpy dependency required for cdist/cpdist return types
No documented SPDX license identifier in pyproject.toml (only 'MIT' string)
